title: K=32 coverage diagnostic for product-key persistent-state addressing
question: Does expanding the product-key shortlist from K=16 to K=32 close the remaining target-recall gap without reverting to exhaustive 64-state scoring?
hypothesis: The K=16 product-key result retains most target states but still loses coverage; a K=32 factor beam should recover additional target states while retaining lower arithmetic than exhaustive cosine scoring.

arms.name: exhaustive_cosine
arms.intervention: cosine-score all 64 persistent states with the fixed width-16 teacher

arms.name: product_key_k32
arms.intervention: same fixed product-key cells and codebooks with factor beam 6 and K=32

decision_rule.condition: report K=32 proposal retention, target recall, end-to-end success, scored states, and arithmetic against the fixed exhaustive reference
decision_rule.licenses: diagnostic evidence about product-key coverage at K=32 on the registered workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: general retrieval guarantees or hardware speedup

decision_rule.condition: K=32 approaches the exhaustive target-recall reference while retaining a bounded shortlist and materially lower arithmetic
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support for larger-budget product-key addressing on this workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: broad C5 or universal semantic memory claims

held_constant: 48 training codes versus 16 held-out query codes
only factor beam and K are changed relative to the K=16 diagnostic
result_note: Full registered run 36699821631: pooled K=32 actual target recall 0.6920 and end-to-end success 0.8280 versus exhaustive references 0.7000 and 0.8333; proposal retention 0.9847; mean query arithmetic 860.28 MACs versus 1,184 exhaustive.
